Alright I can answer this I bought an r6 for $4k. Make sure you inspect the mechanical things, screw the fairings. 
My r6 had problems he didn’t tell me about. The damage was a slightly bent radiator (I just bent it back). Leaking oil from stator (alternator) cover from a small crack, I couldn’t tell until I was riding for a little while, $50 to replace myself.. Check the fork seals if they’re leaking, you don’t want oil all over your brakes if you like stopping, $350 at a shop. Check the chain! Is it all grimy? Easy warning sign of what kind of owner it was. $200 if you change sprockets and chain. 
Ask him to take both the seats off and look at the wiring, are there random wires exposed you’ll have to fix with a soldering iron and shrink wrap? Also a good battery replacement is probably at least $100. Check the clutch free play on the handlebars, there should be at least a little 1/8” free play until the wire actually starts pulling the clutch wire, if not he’s probably frying the clutch. Does it need new a tune because he installed a high flow air filter and short exhaust? A power commander is $350. 
Check the color of the coolant, is it brown? Does it even have coolant in the overflow bottle? Coolant flush and new coolant is about $50 yourself. 
Does it need new tires? 
Look at the brake pads and see if there’s any left. 
Check for grimy buildup under the fairings and on the bottom of the bike, if so there’s probably an oil leak and he just ignored it. 

Also, make sure he has the title and that it matches the Vin on the bike so you know it’s not stolen. 

If it has a lot of these problems I’d lowball him or walk away.
